About

“Duetto” is a research project on the interaction between artificial intelligence and human movement. The idea is to treat the body as a language: body positions become the basic elements, while movements become complex sequences, much like sentences built within a discourse.

But Duetto does not simply describe what the body does. It also tries to recognise relations, possibilities and transformations within gesture. In this sense it works as a kind of intelligent mirror — capable of observing movement, understanding it, and returning new expressive possibilities.

Dance is where the body expresses its complexity most fully. Technique, intention, memory, variation, listening, invention: a living language that holds together rigorous structure and potentially infinite freedom. It is not simply a field of application, but the ideal ground for a system meant to engage with the creative dimension of movement, and not only to read it.

What follows from this is a way of working we call human-in-the-loop: human action does not only come at the beginning, but continuously guides what the system understands and proposes. Artificial intelligence here is neither a passive tool nor a replacement for performers and choreographers, but a creative interlocutor.

Duetto was born within S+T+ARTS, the European programme promoting exchange between science, technology and the arts. It is led by Sony CSL – Rome in collaboration with Centro Coreografico Nazionale/Aterballetto, La Piroetta Dance School/Aleph Dance Company and the European University of Rome.
